history: Found as a live split, and the interesting part was WHY Python refused. Both JavaScript parsers accepted it and agreed byte-for-byte on the canonical form {"\ud800":1}. Python refused by accident: _check_shape called len(k.encode("utf-8")) to apply the string-length limit, and the UnicodeEncodeError that escaped is what refused the receipt -- a side effect of measuring a length, not a rule anybody had written down. canonical_bytes would have handled the value perfectly well. Now stated and applied deliberately everywhere.
note: A key written as the escape \ud800: legal JSON grammar, not legal Unicode, and with no UTF-8 encoding at all. A receipt is a UTF-8 document, so this is not one, and every implementation now says so.
